NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under City Council Meeting agendas at rhe.city and during regular
  business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's website and a
  recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP-TV Channel 35
  (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome in-person on any item during City Council consideration of the item. Public
  correspondence may also be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record. Members of the public may also comment online using
  eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos” page of the City’s website
  (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment” button next
  to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After you
  register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
  public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the record.

  An opportunity is also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If
  you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public
  comment, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  FEBRUARY 27, 2024

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Former Los Angeles County Sheriff Captain James Powers.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Donald Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

**ITEM TAKEN OUT OF ORDER**

B.  PRESENTATION TO FORMER LOS ANGELES COUNTY SHERIFF CAPTAIN
  JAMES C. POWERS ON THE OCCASION OF HIS RETIREMENT

The City Council presented James Powers with a Resolution of Commendation in recognition
of 36 years of service in the Sheriff’s Department, including five years of service as Captain at
Lomita Station.

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MARCH 2024 AS WOMEN'S HISTORY MONTH

MAYOR SCHMITZ declared March 2024 as Women’s History Month.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO GEOSYNTEC CONSULTING INCORPORATED’S
  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT (PSA) TO PROVIDE ADDITIONAL
  ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR STORM DRAIN REPAIRS ON PALOS VERDES
  DRIVE EAST (PVDE) IN CONJUNCTION WITH A DRY WELL STORM DRAIN
  PROJECT AT PVDE & BRIDLEWOOD CIRCLE

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Approve a Second Amendment to the
  Professional Services Agreement (PSA) with Geosyntec Consultants, Inc. to provide
  additional engineering services for storm drain repairs on the Palos Verdes Drive East
  (PVDE) bridle trail in the amount of $54,900, all to the satisfaction of the City Attorney;
  and 2) Direct staff to solicit bids for the PVDE bridle trail storm drain repair work.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
FEBRUARY 27, 2024
 Director Wahba explained that he was able to negotiate a lower cost by reducing the number
of hours needed on site in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF’s concern about the
increase in staff billing rates.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  1) APPROVE A SECOND AMENDMENT TO THE PROFESSIONAL
  SERVICES AGREEMENT (PSA) WITH GEOSYNTEC CONSULTANTS, INC.
  TO PROVIDE ADDITIONAL ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR STORM DRAIN
  REPAIRS ON THE PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST (PVDE) BRIDLE TRAIL IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $54,900, ALL TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY
  ATTORNEY; AND 2) DIRECT STAFF TO SOLICIT BIDS FOR THE PVDE
  BRIDLE TRAIL STORM DRAIN REPAIR WORK.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

None.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF toured AltaSea with the South Bay Cities Council of
Governments (SBCCOG) last week and attended the Cal Cities State Board of Directors
meeting in Yosemite.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER attended the Palos Verdes Peninsula Transit Authority
Board meeting, as well as the Traffic & Safety Committee meeting last week.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA plans to attend the 9th Annual South Bay Legislative Meet &
Greet on March 1, presented by the SBCCOG, South Bay Association of Chambers of
Commerce, and the LA Division of the League of California Cities. She also indicated there
is an Environmental Advisory Committee meeting on March 6.

MAYOR SCHMITZ attended the Los Angeles County Sanitation District Meeting last week
and highlighted some of the sewer systems failures during the recent large storms.
